    Medical data of almost 19 mln Poles leaked in 'unprecedented' breach

    'Nobody will give in to any blackmail,' says digital minister, pointing finger at cybercriminals.

    Ewan Jones
    Edited by Piotr Kononczuk
     12.08.2026, 17:29
    Share
    FACEBOOK X E-MAIL COPY LINK
    Save
    DOWNLOAD PDF PRINT

    The data of almost 19 million Polish citizens has been leaked in an “unprecedented" cybersecurity incident in which online patient records were targeted, the country's digital affairs minister has said. 


    The information was stored on the MyDr platform, which is one of Poland's largest providers of confidential electronic patient records and is used by doctors, clinics and medical practices. 


    Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said cybersecurity services were working intensively to establish how the breach had happened. 


    “The response has been coordinated, and the Polish government is securing all information related to the cybersecurity incident,” Gawkowski told a press conference on Wednesday.  


    “As confirmed by the company itself, 19 million records were stolen, containing various types of data that can be linked together.” 


    Gawkowski said there were currently no indications that the data was stolen as the result of an attack by another country. 


    ‘No’ to blackmail 


    He added that the breach appeared to be the work of cybercriminals motivated by financial gain and vowed a firm response. 


    “Nobody will negotiate with anyone,” he said. “Nobody will give in to any blackmail." 


    The minister said the public would be informed as the situation developed, but that the first course of action should be for people to secure their PESEL public administration ID number, which can be done through the government’s mObywatel app.
